antipatterns.name: Escape-hatch calibration acceptance
antipatterns.description: Accepting a calibration rule's always-firing fallback branch as evidence the parameter was calibrated, when the fallback fired for every candidate and the tolerance never actually bound.

antipatterns.name: Log truncation on restart
antipatterns.description: A serve/log script that truncates its own log file on every process restart, destroying forensic history (8 of 11 R6 sessions' logs were lost this way) needed for later performance autopsies.

antipatterns.name: Aggregate-score dominance claims
antipatterns.description: Declaring one candidate superior to another from average/aggregate score alone without checking pairwise pass-set overlap, unique successes, or complementarity.

antipatterns.name: Single-clock latency reporting
antipatterns.description: Publishing latency figures from one clock source (e.g. monotonic timers) without cross-validating against an independent realtime source, especially on virtualized or power-managed hosts.

antipatterns.name: Capacity-implies-bandwidth assumption
antipatterns.description: Inferring a workload runs comfortably on hardware because the model fits in memory/VRAM, without separately measuring bandwidth or throughput utilization against the bottleneck resource.

antipatterns.name: Poll-based completion detection
antipatterns.description: Using fixed-interval polling to detect long-running job completion instead of event/signal-driven hooks, adding systematic latency overhead on every run boundary.

antipatterns.name: Collapsed scalar verdicts
antipatterns.description: Reporting a multi-clause gate result as a single pass/fail scalar instead of per-clause, discarding which specific condition failed or passed.

case_studies.name: The cap-tolerance escape-hatch failure
case_studies.one_line: R6's pre-registered generation-cap calibration rule never bound for any of 4 candidates; the fallback (freeze at ceiling) fired 100% of the time, silently becoming the actual policy and driving 41% of the milestone's wall clock into zero-scoring truncated generations.
case_studies.illustrates: A calibration rule's fallback branch must be sanity-checked against the current candidate class before trusting that calibration occurred; reasoning-model output-length growth can invalidate caps inherited from older model generations.

case_studies.name: The R6 performance autopsy
case_studies.one_line: Forensic reconstruction of a 24h experiment's wall clock from ledger, DB timestamps, logs, git, and transcripts uncovered a chronic 8-12% clock skew invalidating years of published latencies, and showed a candidate hardware upgrade would have made the workload slower, not faster.
case_studies.illustrates: Performance autopsy as a project-independent method: multi-source cross-validated critical-path reconstruction plus bottleneck-specific counterfactual costing, done before any hardware decision.

case_studies.name: Silent-failure collapse under a stronger local model
case_studies.one_line: Qwen3.8-27B's raw pass rate barely beat Nemotron's, but its verifier-clean silent-failure count dropped by more than an order of magnitude, converting failures into visible truncations a simple deterministic gate could catch and making a learned router unnecessary.
case_studies.illustrates: Raw accuracy is the wrong single metric for cascade/gate design; what matters is whether a candidate's failures are visible to the escalation mechanism.

case_studies.name: Noise-floor drift across restart probes
case_studies.one_line: A materiality threshold (+5 net all-pass) was set from one restart probe (23/48 outcomes moved, net 0); a later same-config restart pair moved only 6/5 (net +1), showing the 'noise floor' itself varies by config and needs re-derivation, not a one-time measurement.
case_studies.illustrates: Any significance/materiality threshold used in an LLM evaluation needs its own measured noise floor per config family, not an inherited or one-off estimate.

gaps_noticed: No statistical power/MDE methodology beyond ad hoc noise-floor probes and threshold deltas; 04-experiment-stats needs dedicated power-analysis guidance from elsewhere.

No deployment/rollout guidance beyond local single-server serving; 10-deployment chapter is thin from this source set.

antipatterns.name: Composite AI productivity score
antipatterns.description: Building one scalar 'productivity' metric from token/tool-call volume; D0 and H0-H3 both explicitly prohibit this because it invites Goodharting and conflates activity with outcome.

antipatterns.name: Undocumented internals scraping
antipatterns.description: Scraping a vendor agent's undocumented internal state to fill in missing telemetry fields instead of recording the signal as 'unavailable' (D0 adapter rule).

antipatterns.name: Auto-promoting ephemeral capabilities
antipatterns.description: Automatically converting a runtime-generated tool/plugin into durable trusted platform configuration without a separate review/promotion pipeline (H0-H3 core architectural principle).

antipatterns.name: Small-sample cross-agent verdicts
antipatterns.description: Declaring 'Agent X beats Agent Y' from a handful of tasks without a minimum sample threshold and task-class stratification (D0 risk table).

antipatterns.name: Model-only capability attribution
antipatterns.description: Attributing all agentic performance to the base model while ignoring harness/context/tool/verifier contribution, collapsing model and harness differences into one number (H0-H3 thesis).

antipatterns.name: Raw model-fit sizing
antipatterns.description: Sizing a local model deployment by whether weights fit in memory alone, ignoring KV-cache/context/concurrency and coexistence with other workloads on the same machine (MacBook guide).

antipatterns.name: Historical-vs-new causal comparison
antipatterns.description: Comparing a historical run's results against a new run's results to support a causal claim about an intervention, when session/environment state can drift between runs — confounds the intervention with the session.

antipatterns.name: Completion-as-success proxy
antipatterns.description: Treating a model finishing/completing an output (no truncation) as evidence of correctness and letting that proxy alone justify a GO decision, without scoring against ground truth.

antipatterns.name: Zero-denominator ratio coercion
antipatterns.description: Silently reporting a ratio metric as 0% (or omitting it) when its denominator is zero, instead of flagging UNDEFINED — hides a data-sufficiency failure as a negative result.

antipatterns.name: Success-gated persistence
antipatterns.description: Only persisting a model's output/trajectory when it parses successfully, which systematically deletes exactly the failure population most needed for diagnosis.

antipatterns.name: Bypassing a fail-closed gate for convenience
antipatterns.description: Running an experiment outside or around a state machine's guardrails because the immediate need doesn't fit an allowed state, instead of adding a narrow, tested extension.

antipatterns.name: Filename/port/alias as model identity
antipatterns.description: Treating a model's filename, serving port, or alias as its identity for reproducibility, when the same name can point at different artifact/runtime/config combinations over time.

antipatterns.name: Single-layer ground-truth protection
antipatterns.description: Protecting an answer key with only one enforcement layer (e.g. an app-level filter) instead of an independent second layer (e.g. a DB role with no grant), leaving one bug away from a leak.

antipatterns.name: Hand-authored 'depicted' failure scenarios
antipatterns.description: Simulating a failure mode by writing the buggy end-state directly into a data store instead of producing it through the real mechanism under test — teaches the shape of a bug without the system ever being able to actually fail that way.

antipatterns.name: Substring/keyword claim matching without polarity
antipatterns.description: Scoring a claim as asserted whenever its keywords appear in text, without checking negation or directionality — rewards or punishes the opposite of what was actually said.

antipatterns.name: Ungated, uncounted access to a held-out evaluation set
antipatterns.description: Letting any experiment read/report held-out TEST outcomes without a pre-registered counting convention and ledger, risking silent over-consumption of a non-renewable resource.

antipatterns.name: Reactive purchase-trigger adjustment
antipatterns.description: Changing or firing an already-defined spend trigger because one favorable piggybacked measurement appeared, instead of waiting for the pre-committed condition to actually be met.

case_studies.name: The Clock That Ran Backward (S04)
case_studies.one_line: Hand-authored 'simultaneous' vendor timeouts were secretly a month apart because scenario generation ticked a shared clock per customer added.
case_studies.illustrates: Mechanistic/emergent test generation surfaces latent generator bugs that scripted depictions of the same scenario would hide.

case_studies.name: The Ledger Sort That Hid a Race (S07)
case_studies.one_line: Sorting a ledger tool by event time instead of posting order made a real reversal race look like a clean, net-zero ledger, until the fix raised the arm's score 0.125→1.000.
case_studies.illustrates: A query tool's sort order/column list is part of its semantic contract; a subtly wrong shape can make a class undiagnosable and masquerade as model weakness.

case_studies.name: The Customer-Keyed Tool That Made Clustering Impossible
case_studies.one_line: A verification-lookup tool keyed only by customer_id made a cross-customer vendor-outage class categorically unsolvable (0% accuracy) until it gained cohort-level parameters.
case_studies.illustrates: Before scoring a cohort-defined task, verify a tool actually exposes cohort-level access, or the class is impossible by tool shape, not difficulty.

case_studies.name: 312 Unreachable Deliveries
case_studies.one_line: Zero of 312 webhook deliveries had a tool-reachable event id, silently capping four scenario classes below the recall threshold before any model was scored.
case_studies.illustrates: Rule out harness-imposed recall ceilings via a reachability check before attributing eval failure to the model.

case_studies.name: The Proxy That Reordered JSON Keys
case_studies.one_line: A routing gateway's key-sorting reserialization silently broke an order-sensitive grammar compiler, producing 0/48 identical outputs versus the direct path until an order-invariant schema rewrite fixed it.
case_studies.illustrates: Verify byte-level request equivalence when inserting a new transport hop into a controlled comparison; passthrough is not automatically neutral.

case_studies.name: Two Forks, One Constant, Different Geometry
case_studies.one_line: Two llama.cpp runtime forks both defined the same enum value for a quantization type with different block layouts; only a full runtime digest distinguished them.
case_studies.illustrates: Filename/build-name identity is insufficient for reproducibility; digest the actual runtime binary and its mapped libraries.

case_studies.name: The Substring Scorer That Punished Correctness
case_studies.one_line: A forbidden-claims scorer counted a refutation ('not caused by insufficient funds') as an assertion of the claim, costing a correct answer 8 points before a polarity-aware rewrite.
case_studies.illustrates: A rule-based grader must be negation/polarity-aware and directionally scoped, or it silently rewards the wrong behavior.

case_studies.name: M0: The Diagnostic That Gates the Expensive Run
case_studies.one_line: A ~$4, one-day paired-probe diagnostic on 15 TRAIN cases, with a precedence gate for data sufficiency over effect size, decides whether to spend 18-22 hours on a full calibration experiment.
case_studies.illustrates: Gate an expensive experiment behind a cheap, pre-registered diagnostic whose primary metric — not completion or proxy signals — drives GO/RE-SCOPE/DROP, with data-sufficiency checked before effect size.

case_studies.name: The Rental Credentials That Didn't Exist
case_studies.one_line: A pre-registered GPU-rental benchmark reached execution before discovering no rental account/credentials existed in the lab environment; the ledger recorded it as 'NOT RUN' with reason, not silently dropped.
case_studies.illustrates: Verify environment/access prerequisites exist before pre-registering dependent work; record blocked attempts honestly rather than omitting them.

case_studies.name: Restart Instability and the Case for Paired Controls
case_studies.one_line: 23 of 48 case outcomes moved across a server restart, which is why M0 uses a same-session paired control instead of trusting a historical-vs-new comparison.
case_studies.illustrates: Measure session-to-session instability before trusting any comparison spanning separate sessions; prefer contemporaneous paired controls.

statements.underlying_generic_rule: Any deterministic text-matching scorer for claim/negation detection needs symmetric context, sentence-boundary awareness, and boundary-condition fixture tests, not just positive cases.

statements.statement: A verifier's set of fields the model could have observed must be kept in exact sync with everything the tool outputs actually expose, or legitimate citations get scored as fabrications.
statements.evidence: collect_observed_ids missed idempotency_key though get_webhook_history returned it
statements.underlying_generic_rule: A verifier's allowlist of observable/citable fields must be derived from and tested against the actual tool output schema, not maintained by hand separately.

statements.statement: Every scored artifact must persist an explicit instrument-version identifier; comparison tooling must refuse to mix versions unless explicitly overridden, printing a caveat.

statements.statement: Prove corpus/data-generation determinism as a release gate: regenerate the full corpus independently and compare a canonical content digest.
statements.evidence: make corpus-determinism: two regenerations, identical per-split digests

statements.statement: Before scoring any model, compute each task class's reachability ceiling by replaying the evidence plan against the built corpus; a below-threshold ceiling is an instrument defect, not model difficulty.
statements.evidence: make reachability computes recall ceiling per class on built corpus

statements.statement: A low score on a task class can mean the class is unwinnable (reachability ceiling below threshold), not that the model is weak.
statements.evidence: 5 of 12 classes had ceiling 0.25-0.50 before fix; 'scores looked like a weak model'
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Always compute per-class reachability/ceiling before attributing a low score to model weakness; a low ceiling means the instrument, not the model, is failing.

statements.statement: Required gold evidence must: exist in the generated instance, be reachable through the model's actual tool surface, and have reachability empirically demonstrated on the built corpus, not just argued.

statements.statement: A retrieval/tool simulator that selects by non-unique keys risks results crossing scenario boundaries; constrain addressing so lookups can't leak across cases.

statements.statement: Cross-check a synthetic-data generator's output against an independent replay of the real downstream consumer logic; require id-set and field-level agreement as a release gate.

statements.statement: Structure a diagnostic/investigation task ontology as four closed, versioned layers: presenting symptom category, root-cause diagnosis, sanctioned next action, and forbidden harmful claims.
statements.evidence: task-ontology.md §1-4 structure

statements.statement: Design some symptom categories to map to multiple root causes so a shortcut lookup solution is capped well below full accuracy, and document the expected shortcut ceiling.
statements.evidence: 3 of 8 categories deliberately ambiguous; 'lookup model will score ~50%'

statements.statement: Treat an assertion as forbidden (fails the case outright) when believing it would trigger a costly or harmful real-world action, distinct from ordinary uncited/incorrect claims.
statements.evidence: task-ontology.md §4: 'claim that would trigger a costly or harmful real-world action if believed'

statements.statement: Closed label sets scored by exact match: adding, removing or remapping any member is a breaking change requiring an explicit version bump and rationale log entry.
statements.evidence: task-ontology.md §2,§6: root cause/action set changes bump SUITE_VERSION

statements.statement: When a decision policy is both taught to the model in-context and used to grade it, keep the two copies in sync via a single source of truth or an automated equality test.
statements.evidence: CAUSE_TO_ACTION in prompts.py and manifests; test_prompt_table_matches_the_rubric fails on drift

statements.statement: On a two-stage task, split second-stage accuracy by whether the first stage was correct; near-identical accuracy either way means the bottleneck is stage two.
statements.evidence: action accuracy 18.8% when root cause correct vs 17.5% when wrong — identical
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Diagnose which stage of a multi-step task is the true bottleneck using conditional (stage-2 | stage-1 outcome) accuracy before designing an intervention.

statements.statement: Making an implicit closed vocabulary/mapping explicit in the model's prompt can produce large accuracy gains where inference of the mapping was the actual bottleneck.
statements.evidence: cause→action table in prompt: 18.8%→100%; listing root causes: 18.8%→60.4%
statements.fis_specific_values: E6 intervention variant D specific percentages
statements.underlying_generic_rule: If evaluation shows a model cannot reliably infer a closed mapping/rule it needs, put the mapping explicitly in-context rather than relying on inference or scale.

statements.statement: Keep a closed-set distractor option that is never currently correct to measure whether a model reasons or anchors on surface names; don't remove it reactively.
statements.evidence: replay_webhook sanctioned for no root cause, retained as deliberate distractor, decision logged 2026-08-15

statements.statement: When a model's answer looks defensible against the rubric, investigate whether the disagreement reproduces on clean data before changing the rubric; close only when a separate defect explains it.
statements.evidence: task-ontology.md 'Two entries reviewed and CLOSED': re-checked on suite v2, E4 96/96 sanctioned

statements.statement: Never widen a scoring rubric because a model disagreed with it, and never narrow it because a model now agrees; a change must rest on an independently identified instrument defect.
statements.evidence: task-ontology.md and contract §8: 'never widen the rubric in response to model answers'

statements.statement: Every element of a model-facing closed taxonomy must have at least one generative/reachable scenario pathway; test coverage so no label is a selectable-but-never-correct trap.
statements.evidence: test_table_has_no_causes_the_corpus_never_generates

statements.statement: Ontology changes follow a fixed checklist: bump version, update every synchronized copy, re-check reachability for new classes, log rationale, never compare silently or react to one model's answers.
statements.evidence: task-ontology.md §6, six-step change procedure

statements.statement: Set a partial-credit evidence/citation recall threshold below 100% rather than requiring perfect citation, and hold it fixed across baseline comparisons.
statements.evidence: 'the 0.8 recall threshold' unchanged across suite versions

statements.statement: Report quality metrics and performance/cost metrics together per arm in every baseline, not quality alone.
statements.evidence: contract §6 Metrics table: quality + performance recorded per DEV/TEST arm

statements.statement: Record full run provenance (commit, instrument version, corpus digest, model/checkpoint/quant, decoding params, runtime build, session identity) with every scored run.
statements.evidence: contract §6 'Recorded per arm', runtime_context/ModelInvocation

statements.statement: Before trusting per-case results from an eval run, re-run the same configuration and require near-total agreement on output digests/outcomes; stop for diagnosis if not met.
statements.evidence: Qwen A vs B reproducibility gate ≥46/48 required before per-case reading

statements.statement: Treat a single run of a non-deterministic, unseedable model configuration as one sample, not a baseline to be cleaned up by re-running; only re-run if the harness changed afterward.
statements.evidence: contract §6: frontier sanity run doubles as baseline iff no suite change follows

statements.statement: Hold a held-out test split completely untouched until an explicit freeze point, then run it exactly once per frozen configuration with no further tuning after seeing results.
statements.evidence: contract §7 DEV/TEST policy; report §7 'nothing tuned or re-run after seeing TEST'

statements.statement: Size a model's output-token budget empirically per model against measured truncation rate rather than copying another model's budget; architectures differ in this need.
statements.evidence: Qwen 4096 fine (1 cap-hit); Nemotron 4096 truncated 29/48, needed 8192

statements.statement: A raw score difference between two instrument versions is not a causal model-capability measure; decompose it into removed false-failures, removed defensible-wrong readings, and genuinely different evidence.
statements.evidence: report §8: 'a v3-v2 difference...mixes (a)...(b)...(c)...none of those is the model changing'

statements.statement: When comparing two arms across many cases, use a 2x2 pass/fail matrix, and manually review every case where a weaker/cheaper arm passes and a stronger arm fails.
statements.evidence: report §5 migration matrix; 'every weak>strong inversion harness-reviewed'

statements.statement: In a routing/cascade system, distinguish silent (gate-clean but wrong) failures from loud ones; gate blindness to silent failures can be the dominant capability gap.
statements.evidence: gate accepts 47/96 and 26/96 verifier-clean-but-wrong; ceiling 99%, delivered 50-72%
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Measure silent (gate-clean, wrong) vs loud failures before assuming more model capability or tuning fixes an underperforming routing gate; the gate itself may be the bottleneck.

statements.statement: A router/classifier choosing between cheap and expensive model tiers must be trained/selected only on production-available features, never on any ground-truth-derived field, enforced by an automated leakage test.
statements.evidence: report §10 R5 plan: router_signals gold guard, test_routing_no_gold_leak

statements.statement: Using a vendor-managed CLI/wrapper instead of a raw API, verify what its cost/token telemetry captures; treat under-instrumented costs as a floor, not an exact figure.
statements.evidence: frontier CLI reports no runtime fingerprint/seed, under-reports input tokens; 'strong cost is a floor'
statements.underlying_generic_rule: When cost/telemetry comes from a managed CLI or wrapper rather than a raw API, verify what is actually instrumented and label the resulting numbers a floor, not an exact figure.

statements.statement: Explicitly record known, intentionally-unfixed instrument limitations in the release document rather than silently living with or overclaiming past them.
statements.evidence: contract §9 and report §9 'Known limitations left intentionally unfixed (recorded now)'

statements.statement: Correct a post-release factual error via a dated errata addendum that explains the correction without altering any originally published number.
statements.evidence: report §11 Errata: bucketing correction recorded 2026-08-18, table numbers unchanged

statements.statement: Nothing derived from a real employer/client system — code, schemas, prompts, architecture, credentials, or 'inspired by' reconstructions — may enter a reusable/portfolio research artifact.
statements.evidence: clean-room-boundary.md 'The rule'

statements.statement: Distinguish reusable public 'shape' (industry-standard concepts) from prohibited employer 'specifics' (actual schemas, contracts, logic) when deciding what may go into a public artifact.
statements.evidence: clean-room-boundary.md shape-vs-specifics table

statements.statement: Use the test 'could I have written this having never worked at the employer, using only public documentation?' as the decision heuristic for any IP/provenance question.
statements.evidence: clean-room-boundary.md 'If in doubt'

statements.statement: Enforce privacy/provenance guarantees structurally in code and schema (no PII fields, placeholder tokens, fictional generators) rather than relying only on procedural review.
statements.evidence: clean-room-boundary.md: no PAN field in schema, no SSN/address/phone/email fields exist

statements.statement: Build data-residency/policy enforcement (a policy tag refused for non-approved destinations) before any sensitive data exists, so enabling real data later is a config change, not a re-audit.
statements.evidence: DataPolicy + ModelAdapter._check_policy refuses LOCAL_ONLY to non-local provider, nothing marked yet

statements.statement: For agentic/tool-using systems near systems of record, enforce read-only/no-side-effect boundaries at the lowest feasible layer, not only in application logic.
statements.evidence: fis_tools DB role is default_transaction_read_only at the connection level

statements.statement: In consequential/regulated-adjacent domains, keep AI output as recommendation codes for a human to execute, and state the system's non-capabilities explicitly.
statements.evidence: clean-room-boundary.md 'AI tools are read-only'; 'not an AML/KYC decision system'

statements.statement: When extracting a reusable platform from a domain-specific project, classify each component as transferable-as-is (gateway, schemas, verifier, eval runner, taxonomy) versus domain content to discard entirely.
statements.evidence: clean-room-boundary.md 'Reusable vs domain-specific' table

statements.statement: Direct-write generation paths that bypass the real event pipeline (e.g., writing a ledger entry straight into state) are deprecated and removed; do not reintroduce direct-insert shortcuts.
statements.evidence: World.add_entry and World.entries deleted, ledger.entries removed from generator's _TABLES

case_studies.name: Reachability Ceiling Blind Spot
case_studies.one_line: A structurally unwinnable task (0.25-0.50 recall ceiling in 5 of 12 classes) was mistaken for model weakness until ceiling was measured directly against the built corpus.
case_studies.illustrates: Validate the instrument's achievable ceiling before attributing a low score to model capability.

case_studies.name: Cause-to-Action Prompt Table (E6)
case_studies.one_line: Action accuracy was ~18% regardless of whether the model's own diagnosis was right or wrong; making the diagnosis-to-action mapping explicit in-prompt took it to 100%.
case_studies.illustrates: Use conditional (stage-2 given stage-1) accuracy to locate the true bottleneck stage of a multi-step task before intervening.

case_studies.name: Suite v3 Defect Discovery via Arm Disagreement
case_studies.one_line: Four independent harness/scorer/verifier defects (pipeline-bypass fingerprints, balance inconsistency, scorer window bug, verifier field gap) were found by treating cross-arm disagreement as a signal to investigate, not to score.
case_studies.illustrates: Cross-arm/model disagreement is a detection mechanism for instrument defects; fix and version the instrument, never the model's score.

case_studies.name: Silent-Failure Gate Blindness
case_studies.one_line: After the instrument was validated, the largest remaining gap (50-72% delivered vs 99% achievable) was traced to the routing gate accepting verifier-clean wrong answers, not to model capability.
case_studies.illustrates: Once instrument validity is established, use silent-vs-loud failure analysis to find the real next bottleneck before adding model capability or tuning.

gaps_noticed: These docs show ontology -> corpus -> validated instrument -> versioned release well, but not the earlier step of deriving a task ontology from a business/stakeholder requirement in the first place — the ontology is presented as already-existing/closed; only 'how to change it' is covered.

No general guidance on statistical significance, confidence intervals, or minimum detectable effect for the pass-rate deltas reported here (raw counts/percentages only) — likely covered elsewhere, absent from this document set.

No treatment of how to build a validated instrument for tasks without a synthetic-data generator (e.g. real-world evals requiring human-annotated gold and inter-rater agreement) — the reachability/determinism apparatus here assumes a code-driven generator.
No decision criteria for how much instrument-validation investment (reachability ceilings, determinism gates, corpus digests) is proportionate for a smaller or lower-stakes project than this one.
The 'forbidden claim = costly/harmful if believed' test is stated but not generalized to domains where real-world consequences are less clear-cut than fintech's fraud/SAR/account-freeze examples.

antipatterns.name: Score-driven harness changes
antipatterns.description: Modifying a benchmark's scorer, verifier, or rubric because of what a specific model's score looks like, rather than because of a proven, independently-justified instrument defect.

antipatterns.name: Pipeline-bypass data generation
antipatterns.description: Writing synthetic scenario data (especially background/distractor data) directly into state instead of through the same pipeline real events go through, leaving model-visible artifacts that leak the answer.

antipatterns.name: Cross-version score subtraction
antipatterns.description: Subtracting or diffing raw pass rates between two versions of an eval instrument and reporting the delta as a model-capability change.

antipatterns.name: Ceiling-blind scoring
antipatterns.description: Reporting and interpreting per-class accuracy without first computing the class's reachability ceiling, so an unwinnable task looks like model weakness.

antipatterns.name: Rubric drift from results
antipatterns.description: Widening a rubric because a model disagreed with it, or narrowing it because a model now agrees, without an independently identified generation/harness defect.

antipatterns.name: Gold leakage into production-facing features
antipatterns.description: Training or selecting a router/classifier used at inference time on any field derived from ground truth, rather than only production-available signals.

antipatterns.name: Cherry-picked non-deterministic baseline
antipatterns.description: Re-running a non-seedable model configuration repeatedly to obtain a cleaner-looking baseline, instead of treating each run as one sample fixed in advance.

antipatterns.name: Unaudited managed-tool cost accounting
antipatterns.description: Reporting a vendor CLI/wrapper's cost or token numbers as exact figures without checking what the tool actually instruments, when it demonstrably under-reports.

antipatterns.name: Silent instrument-version mixing
antipatterns.description: Joining or comparing eval run rows against manifests/corpora from a different instrument version without an explicit, caveated override.

antipatterns.name: Employer-specifics leakage into reusable artifacts
antipatterns.description: Including any employer- or client-specific schema, logic, prompt, or 'inspired by' reconstruction in a public/reusable research artifact, even when the general domain category is public knowledge.

antipatterns.name: Train-to-compensate
antipatterns.description: Fine-tuning a model to work around broken retrieval, stale data, or a buggy tool instead of fixing the underlying system component.

antipatterns.name: Chat-context-as-working-memory
antipatterns.description: Storing task state, decisions, and open questions only inside a growing conversational context instead of explicit versioned task artifacts.

antipatterns.name: Premature multi-model sprawl
antipatterns.description: Standing up many specialist models/tiers before a single model+tools+eval loop is proven end-to-end with a measured reason for each addition.

antipatterns.name: Leaderboard-driven model selection
antipatterns.description: Choosing a model family by generic public benchmark score instead of measuring tool-call correctness and structured-output reliability on the project's own evals.

antipatterns.name: LLM-judge for objectively-testable tasks
antipatterns.description: Using a model-graded judge to score outputs (SQL execution, schema validity, exact match) that already have deterministic ground truth available.

antipatterns.name: Random split on generated scenarios
antipatterns.description: Holding out randomly sampled rows from a seeded scenario generator instead of entire seeds/variations, leaking near-duplicate scenarios into eval.

antipatterns.name: Observability UI as source of truth
antipatterns.description: Treating a trace-visualization tool (e.g. Langfuse) as the canonical trajectory/eval datastore instead of a view over owned schema.

antipatterns.name: Single aggregate score reporting
antipatterns.description: Publishing only a strict all-pass rate without component-dimension scores, hiding which capability a change actually helped or hurt.

antipatterns.name: Complexity-before-evidence
antipatterns.description: Adding Kubernetes, a dedicated vector-DB cluster, RL/SDPO, or per-specialist GPUs before the simpler current layer has a measured, documented failure to keep up.

gaps_noticed: CONTRADICTION: Canonical Architecture v1 §7 names llama.cpp the primary local runtime (Ollama for quick experiments, vLLM only for rented cloud GPU); the MSI/FIS Guide §4 stack table names vLLM primary locally ('when compatible') and demotes llama.cpp/Ollama to fallback/compatibility options. The playbook needs one resolved default plus the criterion for when the other applies.

The two documents give two different failure/discovery taxonomies that aren't reconciled: Canonical Architecture's 13-category Discovery Controller taxonomy (ROUTING/RETRIEVAL/MISSING_KNOWLEDGE/STALE_DATA/TOOL_FAILURE/TOOL_SCHEMA_FAILURE/PERMISSION_FAILURE/PROMPT_FAILURE/MODEL_REASONING_FAILURE/MODEL_CAPABILITY_FAILURE/BAD_RUBRIC/NOVEL_TASK/UNKNOWN) vs the MSI Guide's 9-category FIS failure taxonomy (routing/tool selection/tool result/evidence synthesis/schema/unsupported claim/knowledge/capability/novel scenario). A canonical playbook taxonomy with an explicit mapping is needed rather than picking one silently.

Could not confirm within these two documents whether the E0-E8 experiment matrix is ever described as 'closed.' Repo commit history outside the assigned documents (R6 ledger, 'M0' work-package/WP-A/B/C language, 'paired-probe' harness, cap-hit case terminology) uses a vocabulary that does not map onto E0-E8 labels, suggesting later FIS practice extended or renamed the matrix rather than treating it as fixed — this should be verified against the actual later-phase FIS documents before the playbook presents E0-E8 as final.

Neither document supplies statistical methodology (sample-size/MDE determination, confidence intervals, effect-size thresholds for 'clearly better') despite both prescribing champion-vs-candidate comparisons and a strict all-pass gate — chapter 04-experiment-stats needs this from elsewhere.

Neither document gives a cost-crossover/economics formula for the qualitative 'use cloud when...' criteria (MSI §7) — no $/rental-trigger methodology comparable to later lab decisions; chapter 11-economics-hardware needs this from elsewhere.

Rollback/incident-response mechanics are named only as pipeline stages (shadow→canary→gate/rollback) with no runbook: no trigger thresholds, no rollback procedure, no post-rollback diagnosis loop specified.

Governance treatment of real (non-synthetic) production PII/privacy in trajectory capture is absent — both documents' privacy guidance is scoped to 'use only synthetic data in the sandbox,' not to how a real deployment should handle authoritative-memory PII in the trajectory store.

These two documents are pure prescriptive/design specifications ('I would build X') authored before FIS implementation work, not reports of measured outcomes — hence no case-study episodes could be extracted from them; empirical FIS results live in later run logs/ledgers outside this assigned document set.

statements.statement: The self-improvement loop (use→observe→diagnose→decide→acquire evidence→fix or train→evaluate→shadow→canary→promote/rollback) governs all system change.

statements.statement: Before treating a failure as a training problem, classify competing explanations and find the cheapest experiment that discriminates between them.

statements.statement: Only train the model when evidence specifically shows model behavior/capability is the bottleneck; never train to compensate for broken infrastructure or bad data.

statements.statement: When a small/local model fails, replay identical evidence to a stronger model: passing implies a capability gap, failing implies a system/evidence problem.

antipatterns.name: bad-rubric-drift
antipatterns.description: Adjusting scoring rubric, thresholds, or required-evidence sets after seeing model outputs, effectively tuning the measurement to the results it produced.

antipatterns.name: test-set-tuning
antipatterns.description: Selecting a winning configuration or threshold using the test split, then treating the resulting test score as an unbiased confirmation.

antipatterns.name: phantom-model-weakness
antipatterns.description: Accepting a near-zero or very low per-class score as evidence of model incapacity without first checking whether the required evidence/signal was reachable at all.

antipatterns.name: silent-transport-assumption
antipatterns.description: Assuming an adapter, gateway, or serialization layer is behaviorally transparent without verifying byte-identical output; order- or format-sensitive downstream compilers can silently change behavior.

antipatterns.name: existence-implies-executable
antipatterns.description: Treating a binary found on PATH, or a flag that looks semantically right, as proven functional without invoking it or reading its documented behavior.

antipatterns.name: post-hoc-cell-picking
antipatterns.description: Running several exploratory variants without a pre-registered rule, then adopting whichever cell scored best on the metric noticed first.

antipatterns.name: confounded-regeneration-credit
antipatterns.description: Crediting a specific intervention for an accuracy delta measured across a corpus/benchmark regeneration that changed multiple things simultaneously.

antipatterns.name: unpriced-escape-hatch
antipatterns.description: Writing a pre-registered stopping rule whose escape-hatch clause is not itself bounded or enforced fail-closed, letting a measured tolerance breach proceed anyway.

antipatterns.name: pooled-clustered-significance
antipatterns.description: Computing significance or effective sample size by treating cases drawn from a small number of non-independent classes as i.i.d.

antipatterns.name: keyword-safety-scorer
antipatterns.description: Implementing a harm/forbidden-claim detector as bare substring matching over free text, which scores negations and refutations as the assertion they refute.

case_studies.name: E2 n=12 to n=96 optimism collapse
case_studies.one_line: A 12-case pilot's 41.7% root-cause accuracy fell to 29.2% at n=96, showing how volatile small-sample eval results are.
case_studies.illustrates: Small pilot samples run optimistic; validate at scale before trusting a headline number.

case_studies.name: Harness-bug-as-model-weakness (E2 citation + evidence-hop fixes)
case_studies.one_line: Two infrastructure fixes, with no model change, moved measured root-cause accuracy from 16.7% to 41.7%.
case_studies.illustrates: Audit the evaluation harness before attributing a low score to the model.

case_studies.name: S04's clock-cursor bug erased the cluster it claimed to test
case_studies.one_line: A shared backdating cursor scattered a 'simultaneous outage' scenario's events a month apart, producing a real 0% score for a signal that never existed.
case_studies.illustrates: Synthetic ground truth can be silently absent because of a generator bug; verify the data actually contains the phenomenon before scoring against it.

case_studies.name: E6 variant D isolates the real driver of a diagnostic gain
case_studies.one_line: A cause-to-action policy table appeared to triple diagnosis accuracy; removing only the action column (variant D) showed enumeration, not the policy, drove almost all of it.
case_studies.illustrates: Ablate bundled interventions before crediting either half with an effect.

case_studies.name: E6b's pre-registered rule rejects the best-looking variant
case_studies.one_line: Variant H scored the highest raw all-pass rate of four citation-recovery prompts but was rejected because it failed both metrics of a rule fixed before it ran.
case_studies.illustrates: A pre-registered multi-metric decision rule stops the temptation to adopt whatever looks best after the fact.

case_studies.name: R5's router that learned the template, not the failure
case_studies.one_line: A silent-failure router's apparent skill mostly reduced to four case constants identifying the scenario's task class; held-out-class evaluation (LOGO AUC 0.39-0.61) showed little real within-class signal.
case_studies.illustrates: Check a learned discriminator against a class-identity/prior baseline using a held-out-category protocol before crediting it with detecting the intended signal.

case_studies.name: R6 headline result dissolves under cluster-robust statistics
case_studies.one_line: A +13.5-point model comparison over 96 clustered cases was not significant once accounted for the 12 task classes' non-independence (effective N ~22).
case_studies.illustrates: Recompute significance with cluster-robust methods before publicizing a headline comparison over grouped, non-independent cases.

case_studies.name: R3/R3b token-cap confound manufactures most of a model's apparent edge
case_studies.one_line: One model looked ~80% better at avoiding silent failures under a fixed 4096-token cap; raising the cap to 8192 for both arms cut that to ~24%, most of the effect having been an unfinished-output artifact.
case_studies.illustrates: Vary a suspected confounding configuration factor on every compared arm before crediting a model-level difference.

case_studies.name: .env trailing-newline corruption surfaces as a distant unrelated failure
case_studies.one_line: An unsafe append truncated a subscription OAuth token; the corruption was invisible until it surfaced hours later as a frontier-arm auth failure.
case_studies.illustrates: Validate secret/config files immediately after any programmatic write; corruption can surface only as a distant, unrelated-looking failure.

gaps_noticed: No treatment of live production monitoring/alerting or online observability — all material here is offline pre-launch evaluation.
No treatment of team/staffing process or multi-contributor handoff — the record operates as one operator plus one agent throughout.
No treatment of data privacy/regulatory compliance mechanics beyond a one-line 'no customer data, synthetic only' clean-room rule.
No treatment of model-license compliance when acquiring community-reuploaded weights — only content-hash provenance is covered, not license review.
No treatment of security threat modeling for the tool-calling surface (e.g. prompt injection via tool outputs) beyond DB-role read-only enforcement.
No treatment of canary/shadow production rollout, rollback procedure, or live A/B testing after a model is selected — the ladder stops at offline TEST-split baselines.
No treatment of multi-tenant capacity planning or concurrency/SLA burn under real customer traffic — latency data here is single-user eval only.

statements.statement: Record explicitly what was deliberately NOT changed after each experiment, not only what changed, so later readers can tell a principled decision from a convenient one.

statements.statement: Before trusting a near-zero or surprisingly low score, verify the required evidence or signal was reachable at all before concluding the model failed.

statements.statement: Treat an inversion — a weaker arm outscoring a stronger reference arm on one class — as a sign the measurement is broken, not a capability finding.

statements.statement: Select or tune configuration only on a held-out dev split; run the test split exactly once and never revisit it after seeing the score.
statements.evidence: experiment-log E6: 'Selection on the dev split... winner then runs on test exactly once'

statements.statement: Fix the adoption/selection rule and its numeric thresholds before running the cells the rule will judge, to block post-hoc cherry-picking.
statements.evidence: experiment-log E6b: decision rule registered before variant H was run

statements.statement: Do not adjust a scoring rubric or acceptance criteria after seeing model outputs; log the temptation for review before the next frozen version instead.

statements.statement: Score multiple independent dimensions rather than one pass/fail rate; a single aggregate figure can hide qualitatively different failure modes.

statements.statement: When an intervention changes more than one factor at once, add an isolating variant that removes one factor to attribute the effect to its real cause.

statements.statement: Check accuracy conditioned on a related correct judgment, not only the aggregate; a model can look improved while the underlying reasoning link is absent.

statements.statement: Validate decoding determinism inside the actual serving process; do not assume reproducibility holds across a server restart or new process.

statements.statement: When scaling a generated dataset, add explicit tests asserting global uniqueness of every id space across splits; single-instance tests will not catch collisions.

statements.statement: Compute significance with cluster-robust statistics when cases are grouped into a small number of non-independent classes; per-case treatment overstates effective sample size.

statements.statement: Split data into TRAIN (fit/tune) / DEV (select among pre-registered candidates) / TEST (opened once to confirm the DEV-selected candidate); TEST is sealed until an explicit, logged, one-time unlock tied to the frozen candidate.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §4,14: TEST refuses to run without --unlock-test; second replay refused.

statements.statement: Pre-register a learned/decision component's evaluation in two stages: a structural skeleton (features, candidates, CV scheme, selection-rule shape) fixed before any candidate is scored, then a numeric amendment (thresholds from TRAIN evidence only) fixed before DEV opens; both committed, never silently edited.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §0-1,§12: skeleton commit then §12a numeric amendment before DEV replay.

statements.statement: A pre-registered numeric threshold may be revised after TRAIN evidence only if the revision predates the next split being opened, follows a fixed derivation formula (not eyeballing), and the change itself (old value, new value, reason) is recorded permanently.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §12a-2: R2 caps replaced pre-DEV, both rewrites and rationale recorded.

statements.statement: A null/negative result for a candidate learned component is a valid, reportable outcome; do not suppress it and do not relax selection criteria after seeing DEV/TEST to manufacture a pass.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §1: 'a null result is a valid result'; primary protocol reported null for both models.

statements.statement: When a pre-registered rule's wording admits two readings, apply one but compute and disclose the outcome under both readings rather than silently resolving the ambiguity in the result's favor.
statements.evidence: R5-report §7,§11: 'fewer frontier calls' vs 'fewer unnecessary escalations' tie-break, both readings printed.

statements.statement: For any learned classifier/router trained on data generated from a small number of templates/classes, fit a 'class-identity ceiling' comparator (predicts purely from the offline group label) and compare the candidate against it; performance indistinguishable from the ceiling means the lift is group-identity prior, not within-group signal, until a held-out-group transfer test shows otherwise.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §9/§12a; R5-report §3,§11: prior_class_ceiling comparator, candidates within 0.01 AUC of it.

statements.statement: Test whether a learned component generalizes beyond memorized group/template identity using leave-one-group-out CV; same-group (stratified) CV only measures within-group fit and must be reported with explicitly weaker evidential status, never substituted silently.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §8,§12a: primary LOGO vs secondary stratified, secondary marked 'weaker evidential status'.

statements.statement: Pooled out-of-fold metrics under grouped/leave-one-group-out CV are biased/uninformative when the label is strongly clustered by group (fold base-rate shift dominates); compute per-fold metrics restricted to folds whose held-out group contains both classes.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §12a-Q: pooled OOF AUC 0.24-0.52 (below chance) is not evidence about transfer.

statements.statement: When individually-legitimate, production-observable features jointly and indirectly identify a forbidden group/identity variable, do not assume removal is possible; quantify the indirect identification rate (e.g. leave-one-out nearest-neighbor test) and report all downstream results net of that channel.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §6: 4 case constants identify class for 45/48 DEV cases via 1-NN.

statements.statement: Build a leak-guard test suite for any learned production component: an explicit allowlist plus forbidden-name schema errors, gold-removal invariance tests, extraction-with-no-gold-fields tests, deterministic digested serialization, and an import ban preventing feature-extraction code from importing evaluation/scoring/ground-truth modules.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §6 leak guards 1-9; R5-report §3: 43+64 leak tests.

statements.statement: Restrict a learned component's inputs to features actually computable from what production persists at serve time on every split/environment; features recoverable only from a richer TRAIN-only source may be explored for diagnostics but must never be an eligible candidate.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §9: answer_structure comparator TRAIN-only, 'DEV/TEST cannot compute; informs recommendation only'.

statements.statement: When adding a learned improvement on top of an existing trusted deterministic gate, compose it as an OR (escalate = existing_rule OR learned_risk ≥ threshold) rather than a replacement, so the new component can only add recall and the existing safety net is preserved by construction.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §9: policy form for all eligible candidates is R4_escalate ∨ (risk ≥ τ).

statements.statement: Gate any candidate learned component behind a TRAIN-only eligibility check (minimum out-of-fold discrimination and minimum lift over base rate) before it is allowed into DEV selection; ineligible candidates are still replayed and reported, marked ineligible, never silently dropped.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §10: TRAIN eligibility gate fixed before DEV; ineligible candidates replayed once and reported.

statements.statement: Use a lexicographic, multi-criterion selection rule to approve a candidate over an incumbent: (a) a materially large improvement with a noise floor, (b) a bound against collapse toward the expensive fallback, (c) net quality improvement, (d) a pre-registered tie-break among survivors.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §12: R1-R4 lexicographic rule fixed before DEV.

statements.statement: Define a 'material improvement' floor as the larger of a fixed minimum case count and a fraction of the incumbent's own known defect rate, so the gate scales with problem size but never approves changes too small to matter absolutely.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §12: K = max(3, ceil(0.25*routing_FN(R4))).

statements.statement: Given a small evaluation split, compute and report the probability a random policy with the same operating characteristics (e.g. same escalation count) would also pass the selection/confirmation rule; a pass with high chance-probability certifies non-degeneracy, not information.
statements.evidence: R5-report one-paragraph result & §9: TEST reading met by random escalator with p≈0.59 for Qwen.

statements.statement: Statistical power of a pre-registered gate depends on the specific arm's base rate and sample size and must be computed and reported per arm; do not assume uniform power across models/candidates from one calculation.
statements.evidence: R5-report §9: random-escalator p≈0.59 (Qwen) vs p≈0.04 (Nemotron) under the identical rule.

statements.statement: A threshold chosen by optimizing a bare utility function (catches minus unnecessary actions) degenerates to a trivial extreme when the base rate crosses the function's break-even point; record this as a known property before selection and rely on a separate bound to reject the degenerate solution.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §10: 'known property... a weakly-ranked router's τ* sits at the grid floor' when base rate > 0.5.

statements.statement: Before investing in a learned routing/decision component, measure the paired-oracle opportunity map between cheap and expensive tiers (both-succeed / rescueable / inversion / both-fail) to establish whether routing is economically meaningful and the ceiling any router can reach.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R2: paired outcome matrix, 58.3% rescueable, 'routing is economically meaningful, proceed to R4'.

statements.statement: Before trusting an aggregate rate difference between two arms as behavior, manually review the individual disagreement cells; harness/scorer/corpus defects are frequently the true cause and reviewing them can surface bugs no aggregate comparison would reveal.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R2: harness review of 4 disagreement cases found 3 real corpus/scorer defects.

statements.statement: When harness/scorer/corpus review corrects some disagreement cases, report both as-measured and review-corrected numbers side by side; never overwrite the raw figure, and never patch the running scorer/corpus mid-baseline (defer to next versioned release).
statements.evidence: routing-exp R2: 'Reported alongside, not instead of, the as-measured figures... nothing changed.'

statements.statement: Build a decision/routing signal only from production-observable proxies available at inference time; eval-only metrics requiring ground truth (e.g. evidence recall against gold) can define training labels/diagnostics but must never be a serve-time input feature.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R2/R4: evidence recall 'eval-only'; production proxies are verifier failure, no-output, unsupported claims.

statements.statement: Before comparing model/config variants on a metric that could be capped by an operational constraint (context length, decoding budget, timeout), run a dedicated one-factor experiment varying only that constraint; a large share of an observed delta can be a constraint artifact, not a model difference.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R3b: max_tokens 4096→8192 isolated as the sole factor, both weak arms.

statements.statement: When claiming an infrastructure change (proxy, adapter, routing hop) is behaviorally transparent to a model, verify by paired same-session runs comparing exact output digests case-by-case, not by asserting semantic/schema equivalence; structured-decoding pipelines can change output from cosmetic differences.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R1: 0/48 digests equal, 14/48 outcomes changed despite byte-length-equal request.

statements.statement: Establish a reproducibility floor before trusting any comparative claim: rerun the identical control (same model/config/session/order) and measure digest- and outcome-level agreement; treat any effect below that floor as noise.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R1,R3,R3b: direct-vs-direct / A-vs-B controls run before every comparative claim.

statements.statement: Case-level (per-example) comparisons across inference runs are valid only within one server session and identical request order when the serving stack has request-order-dependent state (KV/prompt cache, batching); cross-session aggregate rates can still be compared even when individual cases cannot.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R1: same-session 48/48 outcome-identical; cross-session 23/48 scored outcomes differ, tokens identical.
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Any inference/serving stack with order- or state-dependent caching requires session+order control before per-case diffs are trusted; aggregate-only claims are more robust to this than per-case claims.
statements.fis_specific_values: llama.cpp KV prompt-cache, WSL2, pid/boot fingerprints, +4ms transport overhead

statements.statement: Structure nested/prefix escalation policies (trigger-set A ⊂ trigger-set B) so the marginal value of each additional trigger can be measured by simple containment comparison rather than re-deriving a whole new policy each time.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R4: policies none ⊂ parse ⊂ verifier, adopted verifier via bounded-cost rule over parse.

statements.statement: A pre-registered model-swap/upgrade decision should use a multi-criterion checklist (completion rate, quality, individually-reviewed regressions, latency/stability, cost-per-success); a candidate winning on quality alone should not automatically displace the incumbent if it fails any hard operational criterion.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R3/R3b: 5-6 criterion pre-registered checklists, both runs failed on latency/regression despite quality wins.

statements.statement: Opening a TEST/held-out split for one learned candidate is a nonrenewable resource for the whole research program on that corpus; every later candidate evaluated on the same fixed benchmark inherits reduced statistical innocence, and this cost should be stated explicitly before running another such experiment.
statements.evidence: R5-report §9: 'both models' TEST is no longer blind for learned routing on Suite v3; any later router inherits these looks.'

statements.statement: When a residual failure family is shown (via a genuine, pre-registered transfer test) not to be predictable from anything short of the model's own weights, escalate to model-level intervention (fine-tuning/specialization) instead of further routing; use measured predictability, not intuition, to choose the next rung of the optimization ladder.
statements.evidence: R5-report §13: 'model specialization if residual failures are not predictable' — LOGO AUC mean 0.39 found nothing transferable.

statements.statement: Before concluding a cheap lever (prompting) is exhausted and escalating to a more expensive one (routing, fine-tuning), demonstrate exhaustion empirically by running multiple controlled variants against the same pre-registered rule and showing none move the target metric.
statements.evidence: R5-report §13: 'E6/E6b ran eight variants and none moved evidence recall.'

statements.statement: Log routing/gate decisions in production telemetry using only production-observable fields (decision, feature-digest, threshold, risk score) plus join identifiers; never store gold/outcome labels in the decision record itself, join them afterward in a separate analysis layer.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §15: routing_decisions telemetry has production_observable_only=true; gold joined afterward.

statements.statement: Freeze any deployed learned artifact (router, classifier) with a content digest covering parameters, preprocessing, feature schema version, and training lineage; have the runtime fail closed if the artifact's recorded feature schema/order doesn't match the current extractor.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §13: artifact_digest; 'replay and any live runtime fail closed' on schema mismatch.

statements.statement: A learned component's adoption/unlock record should be append-only and refuse a second unlock/replay of the same candidate on the confirmatory split, preventing quiet re-running until a favorable result appears.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §14: 'a second TEST replay of the same policy is refused.'

statements.statement: The routing selection rule's specific numeric constants (K formula 0.25/floor 3; Δ_util caps 20pp/50%; E_max multiplier 1.5; TRAIN eligibility AUC≥0.60/PR-AUC+0.10; threshold grid step 0.05; 12-class LOGO fold count) are FIS project parameters tuned to this benchmark's size and class count, not universal defaults.
statements.evidence: R5-contract §9-12: all listed constants fixed specifically for the 12-class, 48/96-case Suite v3 design.
statements.fis_specific_values: K=max(3, ceil(0.25*FN)); Δ_util=min(20pp,1.5×OOF); E_max=ceil(1.5×OOF×48); AUC≥0.60; grid 0.30-0.80 step 0.05; 12 classes

statements.statement: Implementation detail: llama.cpp compiles JSON-schema 'properties' into an order-enforcing GBNF grammar; rewriting the schema as an ordered allOf list of single-property components survives upstream key-sorting and reproduces a byte-identical grammar/output to the unsorted schema.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R0.1: SwitchyardAdapter.build_body allOf rewrite, grammar(sorted(rewritten))==grammar(plain).

statements.statement: Rejected: a client-side raw GBNF grammar string applied from token one achieves exact request-path output equivalence but was rejected because it silently strips the model's reasoning phase, changing the frozen baseline's decoding behavior even though the new path is byte-identical to itself.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R1: 'grammar applied... from token one: 287 tokens with no reasoning... not adopted.'

statements.statement: On this benchmark, the best learned Qwen router sits within 0.01 AUC of a comparator that reads only the scenario-class identity on TRAIN, and per-fold leave-one-class-out AUC averages 0.39 (near chance) — the router had memorized template difficulty, not learned within-template signal.
statements.evidence: R5-report §11: stratified AUC 0.901 vs ceiling 0.892; LOGO AUC mean 0.39.
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Same as the class-identity-ceiling audit principle: a learned component's lift must be checked against a group-identity-only comparator before being credited as real signal.
statements.fis_specific_values: AUC 0.901 vs 0.892 ceiling; 12 classes; LOGO mean 0.39

statements.statement: Routing a grammar-constrained llama.cpp model through the Switchyard 0.2.0 proxy silently reordered JSON schema keys, which the grammar compiler used to enforce output property order, changing 14/48 scored outcomes even though token/latency/routing overhead were negligible and request content was semantically identical.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R1: 0/48 digests equal, 14/48 scored outcomes differ, +4ms transport overhead.
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Infra transparency claims for constrained-decoding pipelines must be verified by paired output-digest comparison, not assumed from schema/semantic equivalence.
statements.fis_specific_values: Switchyard 0.2.0, serde_json key sorting, GBNF grammar, 14/48 outcomes

statements.statement: Raising Nemotron's token budget 4096→8192 recovered only 6/29 capped cases as genuine correct answers; the rest were revealed wrong or evidence-short, shrinking the originally reported 'silent failures 23→4' (an 80% reduction) to 23→16 (a 24% reduction) once the token-budget confound was isolated.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R3b: RECOVERED_PASS 6/29; silent failures 4 (R3) → 16 (R3b) of 48.
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Isolate operational-constraint confounds (context/decoding budget) with a dedicated one-factor experiment before attributing a quality delta to the model itself.
statements.fis_specific_values: max_tokens 4096 vs 8192, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning IQ4_XS, 29 capped cases

statements.statement: Manual review of the weak/strong/oracle disagreement cells on a 48-case dev split surfaced three real corpus/scorer defects (a polarity window reading only backward past a post-positioned refutation cue; a scenario where a 'forbidden' hypothesis was actually data-consistent; an observed-id collector missing a valid id field) that aggregate pass-rate comparison had silently absorbed as model quality.
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Review disagreement cells, not just aggregate rate deltas, before trusting a benchmark's verdict on model/config differences.
statements.fis_specific_values: S06/S08/S01 case IDs, n=48 dev split, 3 defects found

statements.statement: R5's own retrospective names four concrete pre-registration failure modes on this run: an ambiguous tie-break clause read in the way that picked the lower-quality survivor; a degenerate utility optimum patched by loosening the utilization cap rather than constraining the threshold rule; the primary CV protocol swapped for a secondary one after seeing TRAIN; and low statistical power (p≈0.59) against a random baseline at n=48.
statements.evidence: R5-report §11 'What went wrong with the pre-registration, stated plainly' (1)-(4).
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Log pre-registration failure modes explicitly in the permanent record and carry them forward to the next experiment's rule design, rather than only patching the current run.

statements.statement: The Qwen-frozen policy's TEST confirmation reading was also satisfiable by a same-size random escalator with p≈0.59 (little power), while the Nemotron-frozen policy's failed reading would have been satisfied by a random escalator with only p≈0.04 (real power) — one nominal confirmation rule had very different statistical teeth across the two arms of the same experiment.
statements.evidence: R5-report §9: 'a random 11-escalation would be confirmed with p≈0.04, so the Nemotron reading had teeth and was not met.'
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Compute and report per-arm statistical power of a pre-registered gate; never assume it is uniform across arms/models in the same experiment.

statements.statement: A simple deterministic verifier-based escalation gate (no learned component) recovered about a quarter of the weak→strong quality gap at ~22% strong-model calls with zero unnecessary escalations and ~90% rescue rate, establishing the baseline against which every later routing investment (learned router, model refresh) was measured.
statements.evidence: routing-exp R4: test 29.2%→49.0% all-pass at 21.9% strong calls, 0 unnecessary, 90.5% rescue.
statements.underlying_generic_rule: Measure and adopt the cheapest deterministic intervention first, and require any more expensive intervention to be justified against its measured residual gap.
statements.fis_specific_values: 29.2%→49.0%/50.0% all-pass, 22.9% strong calls, 90% rescue rate, R4 verifier policy

case_studies.name: R5 class-identity ceiling
case_studies.one_line: Learned silent-failure router lands within 0.01 AUC of a comparator that reads only the scenario-class label; leave-one-class-out transfer is near chance.
case_studies.illustrates: Any learned component trained on templated/clustered data must be validated against a class-identity-only comparator, and transfer tested on held-out groups, before its lift is trusted as real signal rather than group-prior memorization.

case_studies.name: R1 Switchyard key-order leak
case_studies.one_line: A 'transparent' proxy reordered JSON keys, silently changing a grammar-constrained model's output on 14/48 cases.
case_studies.illustrates: Infrastructure transparency claims for structured-decoding pipelines must be verified by paired output-digest comparison, not assumed from schema/semantic equivalence.

case_studies.name: R3/R3b Nemotron token-budget confound
case_studies.one_line: An '80% fewer silent failures' headline shrank to 24% once the token-budget cap was isolated as a confound in a dedicated one-factor follow-up.
case_studies.illustrates: Before attributing a quality delta to a model, isolate operational constraints (decoding budget, context length) with a controlled one-factor experiment.

case_studies.name: R2 disagreement-cell harness review
case_studies.one_line: Manually reviewing 4 weak/strong disagreement cases on a 48-case split found 3 real corpus/scorer bugs invisible to aggregate rates.
case_studies.illustrates: Review disagreement cells, not just aggregate deltas, before trusting a benchmark's verdict on model or config differences.

case_studies.name: R5 pre-registration retrospective
case_studies.one_line: R5's own report names four concrete ways its pre-registered rule underperformed in practice: ambiguous tie-break, degenerate-optimum patch, protocol swap, low power.
case_studies.illustrates: Log pre-registration failure modes explicitly and carry the lessons into the next experiment's rule design rather than silently repairing the current run.

case_studies.name: R5 chance-power asymmetry
case_studies.one_line: The same nominal TEST-confirmation rule had p≈0.59 power for Qwen (weak) but p≈0.04 for Nemotron (strong) in the same experiment.
case_studies.illustrates: Statistical power of a pre-registered gate must be computed per arm; a 'confirmed' or 'not confirmed' verdict is only interpretable alongside its chance-baseline power.

case_studies.name: R4 deterministic-gate baseline
case_studies.one_line: A zero-learning verifier-based cascade recovered a quarter of the weak-strong gap at 22% strong calls with zero unnecessary escalations, becoming the incumbent every later routing investment had to beat.
case_studies.illustrates: Ship and measure the cheapest deterministic intervention first; require any more expensive intervention (learned router, model swap, fine-tuning) to be justified against its measured residual.

gaps_noticed: No treatment of online production monitoring or drift detection after a learned router is deployed — the docs cover offline replay and a one-time TEST confirmation but not ongoing post-deployment validation or retraining triggers.

No guidance for setting selection-rule numeric thresholds (K, utilization caps, TRAIN eligibility gate) in a cold-start project that lacks prior TRAIN evidence or an existing deterministic incumbent to measure a 'residual' against.

No discussion of privacy/compliance constraints on what production telemetry may log, even though the routing_decisions telemetry pattern (production-observable-only, joined later) is otherwise directly reusable.
No generalized capacity-planning guidance for running a second model resident for routing/cascade purposes — R3/R3b note GPU/RAM contention anecdotally but don't turn it into a rule.

CONTRADICTION (self-flagged tension, not fully resolved): the R5 contract requires amendments to be derived 'from TRAIN evidence by formulas fixed here' and committed before DEV, but §12a-2's removal of the a-priori utilization caps is explicitly 'audit-driven' and admitted to move 'in the direction of permitting a pass' — the report itself says a skeptical reader should discount the Qwen result for this reason. The playbook should state how to distinguish a legitimate TRAIN-derived threshold amendment from post-hoc threshold-shopping beyond commit-order alone.

The standing rule 'gold labels may score a route but never choose it' (routing-experiments.md) needs an explicit operational definition: R5's own practice is that gold labels legitimately fit/tune the classifier and drive DEV/TEST selection, while only the deployed inference-time decision must read production-observable features only. Worth stating directly rather than leaving implicit.

antipatterns.name: Trusting aggregate rates over paired disagreement review
antipatterns.description: Comparing model/config variants only by aggregate pass rate without manually reviewing individual disagreement cells for harness/scorer bugs, which can silently masquerade as model-quality differences.

antipatterns.name: Assuming proxy/infra transparency
antipatterns.description: Believing a request-path change (proxy, adapter, gateway) doesn't affect model behavior because it is schema/semantically equivalent, without paired same-session output-digest verification.

antipatterns.name: Pooled cross-validation under clustered labels
antipatterns.description: Reporting a single pooled out-of-fold metric from grouped/leave-one-group-out CV when the label is strongly correlated with the group, without per-fold diagnostics on folds containing both classes — the pooled number can be below chance and still mislead.

antipatterns.name: Threshold-only utility optimization
antipatterns.description: Choosing an operating threshold by maximizing a bare utility function (catches minus cost) with no cap, letting it silently degenerate to 'always act' or 'never act' at extreme base rates.

antipatterns.name: Silent post-hoc rule relaxation
antipatterns.description: Loosening a pre-registered selection/confirmation criterion after seeing DEV/TEST results, or resolving an ambiguous rule wording in favor of whichever reading passes, without disclosing both readings.

antipatterns.name: Ungated learned-component adoption
antipatterns.description: Deploying a learned classifier/router into a decision path without a class-identity/group-leakage audit, when its training data comes from a small number of templates or clusters.

antipatterns.name: Ignoring gate power
antipatterns.description: Reporting a pre-registered rule as 'confirmed' or 'passed' without computing what a random/chance policy at the same operating point would have scored under the identical rule.
